dedupe_keys.name: seismic fragility of port components from soil wharf crane interaction modelling gioia tauro

description: This model derives seismic fragility curves for key port components by analysing a pile-supported wharf, the soil beneath it and a container crane on it as one coupled system, which the authors state had not been done before. Ali Güney Özcebe, Francesca Bozzoni and Barbara Borzi of the EUCENTRE earthquake engineering centre in Pavia published it in Infrastructures in 2022. The numerical model is based on the main components of the Port of Gioia Tauro in Calabria, a strategic container hub in one of the most seismically active parts of the Mediterranean. Two-dimensional dynamic analyses produce fragility curves for single components and for the wharf-crane-soil system, and a scenario-based damage assessment compares predicted damage with literature data, showing general agreement despite some variation. Coverage: one port's typical structures, transferable to similar wharves. Access: open-access article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: two-dimensional analyses, a single site's soil and structure, and no calibration against observed earthquake damage. The curves support rapid evaluation of port seismic performance, risk mitigation strategies and earthquake emergency management, that is hazard exposure, emergency response and resilience studies. They complement HAZUS port fragility and the SYNER-G highway and railway fragility curves in the catalogue.
